subject: hand warmer crystals
title: This Liquid Turns to Ice in Seconds, and the Ice Is Hot

scenes.text: This liquid freezes when you touch it, and the ice is hot.
Click the little metal disc inside a hand warmer, and white crystals race through the whole pack.
Within seconds it climbs to about 54 degrees Celsius, almost 130 Fahrenheit.
The liquid is sodium acetate, and it's already colder than its own freezing point.
It's stuck as a liquid until a tiny shock gives the crystals somewhere to start, and freezing releases the heat.
Boil the pack, and the heat goes back in. The same ice, ready to burn again.

description:
Reusable hand warmers hold sodium acetate cooled below its own freezing point of about 54 degrees Celsius.
Click the metal disc and crystals spread through the pack, releasing heat as it freezes. Boiling it melts the crystals and resets it.
Would you call it ice if it's hot?
first_comment: Bonus: the same liquid can be poured slowly onto a crystal and it builds a tower as it falls. What should we freeze next?
